issues.failure_explanation: Since $\psi(a;a)=\phi_\mu(a)=\min(1,a^2/\mu^2)$, the evaluation $\psi(a;a)=1$ used in the case analysis is false whenever $|a|\le\mu$ (there $\psi(a;a)=a^2/\mu^2<1$). That regime is a sub-case of case (2) ($|a|<\sqrt{\mu^2+2\lambda}$), so the chain $\psi(\pm\mu;a)>\psi(a;a)>\psi(\frac{\mu^2}{\mu^2+2\lambda}a;a)$ is only justified after replacing $\psi(a;a)$ by its correct branch-dependent value.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write $\psi(a;a)=\min(1,a^2/\mu^2)$ and verify the case-(2) inequalities separately for $|a|\le\mu$ (where $a^2/\mu^2\le 1\le\psi(\pm\mu;a)$ and $a^2/\mu^2>a^2/(\mu^2+2\lambda)$) and for $\mu<|a|<\sqrt{\mu^2+2\lambda}$.
issues.overall_effect: An intermediate evaluation in the proof of the closed-form proximal map is wrong on part of the domain; the proximal formula \eqref{solutionforproxi} itself remains correct and no later result uses this mis-evaluation.
issues.title: Proximal theorem proof mis-evaluates psi(a;a) as 1
issues.why_classification: The correction is a short routine case check; the theorem statement and all downstream usage survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Define $\rho := \tfrac{1}{2} \min_{i \in \cI_1 \cup \cI_2} \{||\wvx_i| - \mu|\}$. For any $0 < \epsilon < \rho$, the perturbation $\wvx \pm \epsilon \vv$ remains feasible.

issues.failure_explanation: For $i\in\cI_{01}$ (and symmetrically $\cI_{02}$), the claims $|\wvx_i\pm\epsilon\vv_i|\gtrless\mu$ and the resulting quadratic expansions of $\phi_\mu$ are valid only when $\epsilon|\vv_i|<2\mu$; with $\|\vv\|_2=1$ this requires $\epsilon<2\mu$. But the proof only imposes $\epsilon<\rho$ with $\rho=\tfrac12\min_{i\in\cI_1\cup\cI_2}||\wvx_i|-\mu|$, which can be arbitrarily larger than $\mu$ (e.g., an entry $|\wvx_j|=100\mu$ in $\cI_1$ gives $\rho\approx49.5\mu$), and the two final choices of $\epsilon$ also lack a $2\mu$ cap. Moreover, if $\cI_1\cup\cI_2=\emptyset$ (every entry of $\wvx$ equals $\pm\mu$), $\rho$ is undefined. The displayed expansions used to exhibit descent are therefore not valid for the chosen $\epsilon$ as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Additionally require $\epsilon<2\mu$ in both sign cases (equivalently redefine $\rho$ to include a $\mu$-cap, as done in Theorem TH:s-sparse) and handle $\cI_1\cup\cI_2=\emptyset$ by taking any $\epsilon<2\mu$.
issues.overall_effect: The contradiction argument establishing that minimizers avoid $\pm\mu$ has a hole for $\epsilon\in[2\mu,\rho)$ and in the all-breakpoint degenerate case; the theorem statement (and its use in Theorem linearoptcond) is correct once the cap is added.
issues.title: Descent-direction expansions need a missing epsilon < 2mu cap
issues.why_classification: A standard local condition fixes the degenerate regime; the conclusion, method, and all dependent results survive, with no new lemma needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Theorem  \ref{linearoptcond} establishes that $(\wvx, \widehat{\vomega})$ is a minimizer of the model \eqref{constrain_model}.
Thus, $\wvx$ is a local minimizer, proving sufficiency.

issues.failure_explanation: The model is nonconvex and the proof identifies the limit only as a point satisfying the KKT conditions of Theorem linearoptcond, whose sufficiency direction concludes that such a point is a local minimizer. No global comparison of objective values is made anywhere, and nothing excludes multiple distinct KKT/local minimizers, so convergence to "the minimizer" (a definite, global minimizer) is not established; the argument supports at most convergence to a local minimizer depending on the initialization.

failure_location.quote: Then, the sequence $\{(\wvx^{k},\widehat{\vomega}^{k})\}_k$ is bounded and converges to the minimizer of model \eqref{constrain_model} in a finite number of steps.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the statement to convergence to a local minimizer (a point satisfying the KKT conditions of Theorem linearoptcond); the source supports no stronger global claim.
issues.overall_effect: The stated guarantee of finite-step convergence to the (global) minimizer of \eqref{constrain_model} is unestablished; only finite-step convergence to a KKT/local-optimal point is supported. No other formal result relies on the global reading, and the abstract's 'finite-step convergence guarantees' survive.
issues.title: Noise-free convergence theorem claims the (global) minimizer, proof gives a local minimizer
issues.why_classification: The only source-supported resolution weakens the guarantee type from global to local optimality -- a real loss of content -- but the finite-step convergence and all downstream usage survive unchanged, so it is a limited weakening rather than a collapse of the result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Using the update rules \eqref{updateforx_I1} and \eqref{updateforx_I2}, it follows that 
$$ \wvx^{(k_j + 1)}=\wvx.$$

issues.failure_explanation: The per-iteration linear system contains the previous filter $\widehat\vomega^{(k-1)}$, but the claimed limit system replaces it by $\widehat\vomega=\lim_j\widehat\vomega^{k_j}$; convergence of the subsequence $\{(\wvx^{k_j},\widehat\vomega^{k_j})\}$ does not control the predecessor indices $k_j-1$, which may carry a different binary filter. Hence the limit system with the same $\widehat\vomega=\cH_\mu(\wvx)$ is not justified, and the freezing step $\wvx^{(k_j+1)}=\wvx$ -- which requires $\wvx$ to be the unique update generated from the partition $\widehat\vomega^{k_j}=\widehat\vomega$ -- does not follow as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use that the iterates take only finitely many values (each binary partition yields a unique update), so the convergent subsequence is eventually constant; then monotonicity of $\cQ_\mu$ together with uniqueness of the $\vx$-update forces the whole sequence to freeze at a KKT point, legitimizing the limit system and the induction.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-step convergence conclusion of the theorem is not logically established by the displayed argument, although the limit equations and freezing do hold once a missing argument is supplied.
issues.title: Invalid limit passage and unjustified freezing step in noise-free convergence proof
issues.why_classification: All ingredients for the repair (finite-valued iterates, monotone objective, unique updates) are already in the paper, and the fix is a short standard argument that preserves the full conclusion.

The limit identity with $(\mathbf1-\widehat\vomega)\circ\wvx$ and $\widehat\vomega=\cH_\mu(\wvx)$, and the ensuing claim that the whole sequence equals $(\wvx,\widehat\vomega)$ for all $k>K$ (inherited from Theorem covgergalg1's argument), are therefore not justified as written.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: As for Theorem covgergalg1: finite-valuedness of the iterates (unique $\vx$-update per binary partition), monotonicity of $\cJ_\mu$, and uniqueness of the updates imply the sequence is eventually constant, after which the limit identity holds with $\widehat\vomega^{(k-1)}=\widehat\vomega=\cH_\mu(\wvx)$.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence proof of the noisy-case theorem is incomplete at the limit/freeze step, though the conclusion holds once the missing stabilization argument is added.

issues.failure_explanation: The denominator $m-n+\mathrm{card}(\mathcal K+1)$ is non-positive whenever $\mathrm{card}(\mathcal K+1)\le n-m$, i.e., when at least $m$ entries of $\wvx_k$ exceed $c_{k+1}$ -- exactly the regime the continuation strategy is designed to handle. With a positive numerator the fraction is then negative (or the denominator is zero), so the square root is not a real number and $\mu_{k+1}$ is undefined, breaking step 4 of Algorithm continuescheme. In addition, neither Lemma mudecre_objincre (monotonicity of the optimal value in $\mu$) nor Lemma upperbound_lema2_rev (the surrogate identity) entails this formula, so the derivation claim is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a safeguard to the update, e.g., fall back to $\mu_{k+1}=c_{k+1}=\mu_k/\rho$ whenever $\mathrm{card}(\mathcal K+1)\le n-m$ (or clamp the denominator to a positive value), and present the formula as a heuristic rather than a consequence of the cited lemmas.
issues.overall_effect: The continuation scheme can fail to produce a real $\mu_{k+1}$ in the very situation it targets; the fixed-$\mu$ convergence theorems are unaffected since they never use \eqref{updatemu}.
issues.title: mu-update formula has a possibly non-positive denominator and is unjustified
issues.why_classification: A standard local fallback fixes the degenerate case; the heuristic role of the continuation strategy, the algorithms, and all formal guarantees survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the ground-truth nonzero amplitudes span $10^{-2}$ to $10^{2}$. From the paper's own formula the support is $i=1,16,\dots,196$ and the amplitudes range from $\sqrt{200}/(1+e^{96/20})\approx0.115$ (at $i=196$) to $\sqrt{200}/(1+e^{-99/20})\approx14.0$ (at $i=1$). The experiment therefore covers roughly two decades ($\approx10^{-1}$ to $1.4\times10^{1}$), not the claimed four.
